column2: What size of photo, scan, sound or video can I add?
column3: Settings → “📎 Media files”: at most 100 MB (recommended) for an image or a document (25, 50, 100, 200 or 500 MB), and 250 MB (recommended) for a sound or a video (up to 2 GB). A bigger file is refused, with a message saying so (for example “img003.jpg is larger than 100 MB…”). What it means: each file is copied into your family tree, so it takes its room on the disk; full backups (and the copy at a cousin’s) get heavier and slower; opening it needs more memory. The phone over Wi-Fi keeps its own limits. Each change can be undone with “↶ Undo”.

column2: Why don’t “See better”, reading or retouching process a very large image?
column3: To work on an image, the computer unfolds it entirely in its memory: 120 million pixels (12,000 × 10,000) already need about half a gigabyte. Beyond the limit (Settings → “📎 Media files”, 120 million pixels recommended, from 50 to 300), the image is kept and shown, but the server thumbnails, “🎚️ See better”, “✨ Read the record”, the transcription workshop and retouching don’t process it, with a clear message. To process it anyway: raise the limit if the computer has plenty of memory, or add a reduced version of the image.

column2: Read the record: what about notes written vertically in the margin?
column3: A note written at 90° in the margin (bottom to top or top to bottom) is detected: its piece of image is turned both ways, read again, and the surest reading is kept. Its text is no longer mixed with the lines of the record (no more “2”, “1”, “6” in the middle): it comes apart, after the main text, under a “———” line and the title “Margin note:”. If the turned reading isn’t surer, the lines stay as they were read. Lines written normally don’t change.
